nuance: One ending, written attached: 볼수록 (볼 수록 is a spacing error). Doubling with -(으)면 adds emphasis (생각하면 생각할수록). 갈수록 alone = "as time goes on, increasingly". N일수록 = "the more (truly) an N someone is" (전문가일수록 기본을 중시한다). The main clause describes proportional change, often with 더, 점점, or a comparative. No tense goes before -(으)ㄹ수록; past time is marked on the main clause (살수록 …그리워졌다). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 132.

contrasts.note: -다 보면 says continuing leads to an outcome; -(으)ㄹ수록 says two things rise or fall together.

meaning: there's no way that …; … can't possibly …

It expresses strong conviction from what the speaker knows, not from evidence just observed. Spaced: 할 리가 없다. Past events: -았/었을 리가 없다. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 133.

contrasts.note: -나 보다 leans toward a conclusion from evidence; -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 rules one out.

meaning: only if …; (you) have to … for … (a necessary condition); sentence-final -아/어야지: I must / you should
nuance: Marks the first clause as the indispensable condition: 밥을 먹어야 힘이 나지. 만 strengthens it (-아/어야만). With -아/어 봐야 + a negative judgment it means "no matter how much …, it's no use" (말해 봐야 소용없다). Sentence-final -아/어야지 expresses resolve (I must …) or a mild "you should" to others. Unlike -(으)면, which states a plain (sufficient) condition, -아/어야 makes the condition necessary. A command rarely follows -아/어야 directly. After a consonant, 이다 keeps 이 (회원이어야); after a vowel, 여야 (or the uncontracted 이어야). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 137.

contrasts.note: -았/었어야 했다 applies the necessary condition to the past: it should have happened but didn't.

meaning: should have …; ought to have … (but didn't)
nuance: Counterfactual obligation: the needed action didn't happen. It works as self-criticism (내가 더 일찍 말했어야 했어) or as reproach (네가 먼저 연락했어야지). It is firmer than the wistful -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다. The negative is -지 말았어야 했다 (안 -았/었어야 했다 also occurs in speech). Watch the tense placement: -아/어야 했다 primarily means "had to" (일찍 가야 했다 = I had to leave early). With -는데 it can also hint the obligation went unmet, but -았/었어야 했다 makes the counterfactual explicit. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 138.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다 is wistful and self-directed; -았/었어야 했다 is firmer and can blame others.
-아/어야 states a necessary condition; -았/었어야 했다 says it should have been met and wasn't.
-았/었어도 됐다 = "could have" (an open option); -았/었어야 했다 = "should have".

meaning: could have …; it would have been fine to … (but didn't); negated: needn't have …

attachment.form: 안 V-았/었어도 됐다 / V-지 않았어도 됐다

nuance: Counterfactual permission: looking back, an option was open that the speaker didn't take (좀 더 쉬었어도 됐는데). Negated, it says the effort was unnecessary: 이렇게까지 안 했어도 됐는데 ("you didn't have to"), a common gracious response to a gift or favor. -는데 or -(으)ㄹ 텐데 often follows to add regret or politeness. Present permission is -아/어도 되다; -아/어도 됐다 can simply mean "was allowed to (then)". See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 139.

contrasts.note: -았/었어야 했다 = "should have" (an obligation missed); -았/었어도 됐다 = "could have" (an option not taken).

meaning: as (a) …; in the capacity / position of …
nuance: Marks identity, role, or status: 교사로서 책임감을 느낀다. It is often confused in writing with (으)로써 (means, tool, or a time cut-off). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 140.

contrasts.note: (으)로써 marks a means, tool, or cut-off point; (으)로서 marks a role or capacity.

meaning: by means of …; by (doing) …; (with time or count) as of …
nuance: Marks a means, tool, or method (= 을/를 가지고, 수단으로). After a verb, nominalize with -(으)ㅁ and add 으로써: 운동함으로써, 줄임으로써. ㄹ-stems keep the ㄹ inside ㄻ: 만들다 → 만듦으로써 (만듬 is a common misspelling). It also marks a cut-off point in time or count: 오늘로써 10년째, 이번으로써 세 번째. It is formal and written; speech prefers plain (으)로 (대화로 풀자). Don't confuse -(으)ㅁ으로써 (by doing) with causal -(으)므로 (because). meaning: you're saying …?! / to hear that …, … (reacting to something just said or heard)
nuance: A contraction of the quoted -ㄴ/는다고 하다니: the speaker echoes another person's words with surprise, indignation, or disbelief (지금 와서 그만둔다니요?). The form follows the original sentence type: statement -ㄴ/는다니, question -(느)냐니, command -(으)라니, suggestion -자니. As a connective it means "since (I hear) …" plus a reaction (네가 온다니 기쁘다). Contrast the bare-stem -다니 (그만두다니!), which reacts to a fact rather than to someone's words; for adjectives the two coincide (비싸다니). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 142.

contrasts.note: Bare-stem -다니 reacts to the fact itself; -ㄴ/는다니 reacts to what someone said.
-ㄴ/는다니까 repeats your own words with insistence; -ㄴ/는다니 echoes someone else's.

cloze.sentence: 그 비싼 게 {{}}? 말도 안 돼.
cloze.en: That expensive thing is free? No way.
He's telling me to finish all this by today?

nearMiss.hint: You're echoing an order, so use the command form: 하라니.

cloze.sentence: 나한테 왜 화를 {{}}? 그건 내가 할 말이지.
cloze.en: He's asking why I'm angry? I should be asking him that.

cloze.sentence: 그 회사가 이번에 신입을 50명이나 {{}} 한번 지원해 봐.
cloze.en: I hear that company is hiring fifty new grads this time, so give it a shot.

nearMiss.hint: For a reason based on what you heard ("since they say…"), use the quoted form: 뽑는다니.

cloze.en: You're making the cake yourself? I can't wait.

nearMiss.hint: ㄹ drops before -ㄴ: 만든다니.

cloze.sentence: 그 집이 그렇게 {{}} 다른 데 알아보자.
cloze.en: If they say that place is so expensive, let's look elsewhere.

nearMiss.hint: Adjectives take -다니 without -ㄴ-: 비싸다니.

cloze.sentence: 이제 와서 {{}}? 그동안 고생한 게 아깝잖아.
cloze.en: You're suggesting we quit now? Think of all the work we put in.

nearMiss.hint: Someone proposed quitting, so echo the suggestion form: 그만두자니.

nuance.situation: 동료가 "부장님이 내일까지 기획서를 새로 쓰래요"라고 전해요. 황당해서 되묻는다면? (Echoing a relayed order in disbelief.)

options.why: Echoing a command: -(으)라니.
-ㄴ/는다니 echoes a statement; what was relayed is an order.
-자니 echoes a suggestion ("let's"); the director gave an order.

nuance.situation: 친구가 결혼한다는 소식을 다른 친구에게서 들었어요. 기쁜 마음을 표현하면? (Reacting to news you heard.)

options.why: -ㄴ/는다니 = "to hear that …": a reaction to news you heard.
Vowel-final verb stems take -ㄴ다니: 결혼한다니.

meaning: I bet …; probably … (a guess, often gently correcting the listener)
nuance: A fairly confident guess, frequently one that runs against what the listener seems to assume: 지금 가도 문 닫았을걸요. The intonation rises at the end. It is light and conversational, rare in writing, and written attached (갈걸요). In 반말 it looks like the regret ending (할걸), so intonation and context separate them: regret is about the speaker's own past choice and falls; conjecture rises. It is not used to state facts you know. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 143.

contrasts.note: Regret -(으)ㄹ걸 (그랬다) looks back at your own choice; conjecture -(으)ㄹ걸요 guesses about the world.
-나 보다 infers from fresh evidence; -(으)ㄹ걸요 guesses, often from background knowledge.
-(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 denies a possibility; -(으)ㄹ걸요 leans toward it.

examples.ko: 지금 가 봤자 벌써 문 닫았을걸요.
examples.en: Even if you go now, it'll have closed already, I bet.

examples.ko: 민수 씨는 아마 이 얘기 모를걸요.
examples.en: Minsu probably doesn't know about this, I'd guess.

cloze.en: Even if you go now, I bet it's already closed.

nearMiss.hint: The shop has (probably) already closed: past 닫았을걸요.

cloze.en: Minsu probably doesn't know about this.
That movie's probably more fun than you think.

cloze.sentence: 그날은 아마 {{}}. 은행 문 안 열 거예요.
cloze.en: That day's probably a public holiday. The bank won't be open.
That restaurant is probably open by now.

nearMiss.hint: ㄹ-stems take -ㄹ걸: 열걸요 (or 열었을걸요).

cloze.en: If you go up the mountain today, it'll be pretty cold, I bet.

nearMiss.hint: ㅂ-irregular: 추울걸요.

cloze.en: He's probably heard the news already.

nearMiss.hint: ㄷ-irregular: 들었을걸.

cloze.en: If you take this bus, you'll make it on time, I think.

nuance.situation: 친구가 "지금 백화점 가자"고 해요. 밤 아홉 시 반이라 이미 문을 닫았을 것 같아요. (It's 9:30 p.m.; you think it's closed.)

options.why: A confident guess that corrects your friend's assumption.

options.text: 지금 가면 벌써 문 닫을걸 그랬어.
options.why: -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다 voices regret about your own past choice; it can't predict the store's hours.

options.text: 지금 가면 벌써 문 닫았을 리가 있어?
options.why: Rhetorical -(으)ㄹ 리가 있어? means "how could it be closed?", the opposite of what you think.

nuance.situation: 상대방이 "회의 3시죠?"라고 물어요. 확실하지 않지만 4시인 것 같아요. (You think it's 4, but aren't sure.)

options.why: A hedged guess that gently corrects the listener.
-더라고요 reports something you witnessed; it doesn't hedge a guess, and the past tense is off.

meaning: (1) …, what can you do / I'll just … (shrugging acceptance); (2) -았/었지 뭐예요: …, can you believe it (reporting a small mishap or surprise)
nuance: Two uses, split by tense. Present -지 뭐 (polite -죠 뭐): shrugging acceptance of a less-than-ideal option (택시가 없으면 걷지 뭐; 할 수 없지 뭐). Past -았/었지 뭐예요 (반말 뭐야): telling a small surprising or awkward story, often self-deprecating (지갑을 두고 왔지 뭐예요). The polite narrative form is -지 뭐예요, not -지 뭐요. It is purely spoken, often introduced by 글쎄. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 144.

contrasts.note: -고 말았다 states an unwanted outcome; -았/었지 뭐예요 tells it as a wry anecdote.
-아/어 버렸다 marks finality or regret; -지 뭐예요 adds the storyteller's "can you believe it".

examples.ko: 자리가 없으면 그냥 서서 가지 뭐.
examples.en: If there are no seats, I'll just stand. No big deal.

examples.ko: 글쎄 친구 이름을 깜빡 잊어버렸지 뭐예요.
examples.en: Would you believe it, I totally forgot my friend's name.

cloze.en: If the buses have stopped, I'll just walk.
I overslept and ended up late, can you believe it.

nearMiss.hint: The polite narrative form is -지 뭐예요.

cloze.en: If there are no seats, I'll just stand.
Can't be helped. I'll just come back another time.
I completely forgot my friend's name. So embarrassing.
I went to the store, and what do you know, they were having a sale.
I took a wrong turn and wandered around for an hour, believe it or not.
I pretended not to know, but actually I'd heard it all.

nearMiss.hint: ㄷ-irregular: 들었지 뭐예요.

nuance.situation: 친구가 "콘서트 표 매진이래"라고 해요. 아쉽지만 받아들이며. (Accepting a sold-out concert.)

options.text: 할 수 없지 뭐. 다음에 가자.
options.why: Present -지 뭐: shrugging acceptance.

options.text: 할 수 없었지 뭐예요. 다음에 가자.
options.why: Past -았/었지 뭐예요 narrates something that surprised you, and its 해요체 clashes with 가자.

nuance.situation: 동료에게 오늘 아침에 있었던 황당한 일을 말해요. 지하철을 반대 방향으로 탔어요. (A small morning mishap.)

options.why: Past -았/었지 뭐예요: telling a wry anecdote.
Present -지 뭐 is for accepting an option; a past mishap takes -았/었지 뭐예요.
The polite form is -지 뭐예요.

register.source: 글쎄 지갑을 집에 두고 왔지 뭐예요.
accepted: 글쎄 지갑을 집에 두고 왔지 뭐야.

meaning: (the thing called) …, as for …: holds up a concept to define it or generalize; also = N(이)라는
nuance: A contraction of (이)라고 하는 것은: it holds a concept at arm's length in order to define it or make a sweeping statement (인생이란 원래 그런 거야). The main clause is typically a definition or generalization (…이다, …는 법이다, … 것이다). Before another noun, 란 contracts (이)라는 (김민수란 사람, 자유란 말). The idiom N이란 N은 다 means every single N (가게란 가게는 다 문을 닫았다). Its tone is reflective; it is common in essays and aphorisms. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 145.

contrasts.note: -는 법이다 is a typical main clause after N(이)란: a definition followed by "that's how it goes".

examples.ko: 인생이란 원래 뜻대로 되지 않는 법이다.
examples.en: Life never goes quite as you plan.

examples.ko: 오늘 시내에 나갔더니 식당이란 식당은 다 문을 닫았더라.
examples.en: I went downtown today, and every single restaurant was closed.

cloze.en: Marriage is accepting each other's differences.

nearMiss.hint: After a consonant: 결혼이란.

cloze.sentence: {{}} 어려울 때 곁에 있어 주는 사람이다.
cloze.en: A friend is someone who stays by you in hard times.

nearMiss.hint: After a vowel: 친구란.

cloze.en: Life never goes quite as planned.
Every single shop was closed.
Someone named Kim Minsu called.

nearMiss.hint: Same meaning; the cue asks for the contracted 란.

cloze.en: A promise isn't something you make lightly.
Translation is, in the end, a series of choices.

cloze.sentence: 이번 달은 {{}} 주말엔 다 비가 왔다.
cloze.en: This month it rained on every single weekend.

nuance.situation: 어느 문장이 맞아요? (Which sentence is correct?)

options.why: Consonant-final noun + 이란 introduces the concept to define.
After a consonant: 행복이란.
이랑 means "and/with"; it can't introduce a topic for definition.

nuance.situation: 오늘 시내에 갔는데 식당이 하나도 빠짐없이 다 닫혀 있었어요. (Every restaurant was closed.)

options.why: N이란 N은 다 = every single N.
(이)라도 means "even, at least"; the "every single" idiom is N이란 N은.

meaning: because (I was busy) …-ing, (I couldn't / it cost …): an ongoing activity that used up time or attention
nuance: The first clause is an activity that took time or attention; the main clause is what suffered (couldn't do something, was late or tired, spent money) or the effort itself in 수고하다/고생하다 (오시느라 고생 많으셨어요). Both clauses share the subject. Verbs only, with no tense before it (했느라고 is wrong). The main clause can't be a command or suggestion. Compare -는 바람에 (a sudden event, often with a different subject) and -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 (blame). See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 146.

contrasts.note: -는 바람에 = a sudden, often external event; -느라고 = your own ongoing activity ate up the time.
-(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 assigns blame; -느라고 just explains what kept you busy.
-는 통에 blames a chaotic scene around you; -느라고 is your own occupation.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 시험공부를 하느라고 한숨도 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I didn't sleep a wink last night because I was studying for the exam.

examples.ko: 먼 길 오시느라 고생 많으셨어요.
examples.en: Thank you for making the long trip.

cloze.en: I didn't sleep at all last night because I was studying for the test.

nearMiss.hint: No past tense before -느라고: 공부하느라고.

cloze.en: I was playing games, so I didn't do my homework.
I was having so much fun with my friends that I lost track of time.

nearMiss.hint: ㄹ drops before -느: 노느라고.

cloze.en: Thank you for coming such a long way.

nearMiss.hint: Keep the honorific for your guest: 오시느라고.

cloze.en: I'm frazzled from getting ready to move.

nearMiss.hint: -는 바람에 is for a sudden event; ongoing preparation takes -느라고.

cloze.en: I was on the phone and missed my stop.
I was listening to music and didn't hear the doorbell.

nearMiss.hint: 듣- keeps ㄷ before a consonant: 듣느라고.

cloze.en: Paying for the kids' cram schools is breaking my back.

nuance.situation: 버스가 갑자기 고장 나서 지각했어요. (The bus broke down, and you were late.)

options.text: 버스가 갑자기 고장 나는 바람에 늦었어요.
options.why: A sudden external event: -는 바람에.
-느라고 needs the same subject busy with an activity; here the bus broke down and you were late.

nuance.situation: 보고서를 쓰다가 점심을 못 먹었어요. (You skipped lunch writing a report.)

options.why: Your ongoing task ate up the time: -느라고.
No command or suggestion can follow -느라고.
No past tense before -느라고.

meaning: used to …; would (often) … (a repeated habit, usually in the past)
nuance: Describes something that happened repeatedly or from time to time, not constantly: 주말이면 바닷가를 걷곤 했다. It's mostly past (-곤 했다), with a nostalgic or narrative tone; present -곤 해요 = "I sometimes/often …". Verbs only, with the tense on 하다 (갔곤 했다 is wrong). 곤 is the contraction of 고는 and is written attached to the stem (가곤). It is odd with states or one-time events. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 148.

contrasts.note: -는 편이다 rates a general tendency; -곤 하다 recalls recurring episodes.
자주 가던 곳 (modifier) and 자주 가곤 했다 (predicate) both express past habit.
-았/었었다 marks a past that no longer holds, repeated or not; -곤 했다 specifically means repeated.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때는 여름마다 할머니 댁에 가곤 했어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I used to go to my grandmother's every summer.

examples.ko: 그는 생각이 막힐 때면 동네를 한참 걷곤 했다.
examples.en: When he got stuck, he would walk around the neighborhood for a long while.

cloze.en: When I was little, I used to visit my grandmother every summer.

nearMiss.hint: No past tense on the stem: 가곤 했어요.

cloze.en: Whenever things were hard, I would listen to this song.

nearMiss.hint: 듣- keeps ㄷ before a consonant: 듣곤 했어요.

cloze.en: In college we would talk all night long.
I used to play at that playground until sunset.
Even now, I sometimes think back to those days.
Dad would bring home fish-shaped pastries on his way back from work.
When I got anxious, I used to bite my nails.

cloze.sentence: 그는 생각이 막힐 때면 동네를 한참 {{}}.
cloze.en: When he got stuck, he would walk around the neighborhood for a long while.

nearMiss.hint: 걷- keeps ㄷ before a consonant: 걷곤 했다.

nuance.situation: 어느 문장이 자연스러워요? (Which sentence is natural?)

options.text: 어릴 때 저는 키가 크곤 했어요.
options.why: -곤 하다 describes repeated actions; height is a state.

options.text: 어릴 때 저는 동네 도서관에 자주 가곤 했어요.
options.why: A repeated past action: -곤 했다.

nuance.situation: "I'm generally an early riser"(성향)를 말하려면? (A general trait.)

options.why: A general trait rated on a scale: -는 편이다.
-곤 하다 = "now and then I …"; it describes recurring episodes, not your general nature.
